newsitem.title: JAPAN: Insurers approve aid to Nissan Life successor.
newsitem.headline: Insurers approve aid to Nissan Life successor.

text.p: Japan's 43 life insurers officially decided to provide 200 billion yen in financial assistance to Aoba Life Insurance Co, which was set up last month to take over the policies of the failed Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, the Life Insurance Association of Japan said on Friday.

An official at the association told reporters that the 200 billion yen in aid, of which one billion yen will be used as capital for Aoba Life, is expected to be transferred to the company before October.
He also said that the industry does not expect Aoba Life to have any business difficulties in the future.

In April, the Finance Ministry suspended Nissan Life's business because the insurer suffered heavy losses as a result of excessive securities and real estate investments in the late 1980s "bubble era" of inflated asset prices.
The industry last month worked out a framework to deal with the huge losses at Nissan Life, calling on policyholders to accept a cut in guaranteed returns on their policies.
Nissan Life's collapse marked the first failure of a life insurance firm in post-war Japan.

The association official said at the news conference that in the business year which ended on March 31, Nissan Life's liabilities exceeded assets by 59.1 billion yen. It also had 149.3 billion yen worth of unrealised losses from securities holdings.

Including retirement payments to Nissan Life employees and other future expenditures involved in winding up the firm, Nissan Life's actual liabilities will exceed its assets by around 300 billion yen, he said.
